sentence: 16-year-old woman referred to the ophthalmology clinic due to visual difficulty, "like a part of the blackboard that I haven't seen, especially for 3 weeks."
Her mother says that "she has gone from being an active girl to being slow, with difficulty thinking and speaking, and now she sees poorly."
Since she was 7 years old, she has had epileptic seizures that are difficult to control.
Her treatment was carbamazepine, hydantoin and for 3 months she had been taking Topamax 125 mg a day.
The last ophthalmological examination performed a year earlier was normal.
In the examination performed, the spontaneous visual acuity (VA) was 1 in both eyes, with a normal anterior biomicroscopy.
The pupils were isochoric and normoreactive.
The funduscopic study did not show any alterations.
In computerized campimetry, a non-congruent left homonymous hemianopia was observed.
The color test did not show alterations in any eye.
A cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with gadolinium was normal, as was a diffusion MRI.
The rest of the neurological examination was normal.
Due to suspicion of a toxic phenomenon due to Topamax, it was progressively suspended, with subjective improvement in the patient and partial recovery of the visual field.
